parsed.explanation: The combined regime documents multiple traveller-facing exposures. Nationally: passport/visa markers restricted to M/F matching assigned sex, entry officers instructed to refuse on sex doubt and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility, foreign governments issuing travel advisories, a federal ban on trans use of government-funded single-sex facilities, conversion-style federal prison policy, and documented abuse in immigration custody. At state level: facility bans (schools, per dossier; colleges per a third-party assessment), a binary-sex statute, a surgery requirement for licences upheld through 2024, no statewide public-accommodations or hate-crime protection, and polling showing majority support for restrictions. Protections are partial: federal hate-crime and employment rulings, pending litigation, some injunctions, municipal ordinances. No presentation offence or documented in-state violence pattern exists here; the 3.8/100k figure is an unusable undercount floor. Worst features sit at tiers 1–2 with thin state recourse, placing this below 0.35-A.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 executive order and 24 Feb 2025 cable: 'X' markers stopped, M/F only per supporting documents; officers must refuse where documents cast doubt on sex and may consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans travellers report passports confiscated or blocked; at least eight foreign governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing 'X'-marker passports valid until expiration; Supreme Court let restriction take effect but civil-liberties suit remains pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ on documentation strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or fraud finding can strand a visitor before any state-level exposure is reached; the state's surgery-only licence rule compounds document incongruence for anyone carrying local ID.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 federal corrections bureau mandates conversion-style policy (hair cut short, hormones removed, psychiatric substitution); trans immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers in 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender-identity motivated violence; earlier LGBTQ prison executive order rescinded but litigation over related orders continues; an earlier bathroom-law arrest in another state produced charges, showing courts process complaints.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor who is detained — including after an entry-document dispute — enters the federal custody system where birth-sex placement and hormone removal are the operative rules; state-level jail placement for this unit is not documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; state HB322 (2022) requires birth-certificate bathrooms in public schools, a July 2026 assessment extends this to colleges (underlying text unverified), SB79 (Feb 2025) declares a binary and permits separate single-sex spaces; four units nationally criminalise such use in some circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No unit-level protection documented; the mapped 29 units without bans do not include this one; some private settings unaffected, and federal scope is limited to government-funded buildings.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor using a federal courthouse, agency office or campus facility is covered by both the federal order and the state rule; private hotels and restaurants are outside the mapped bans but face no state anti-discrimination floor.

care_services.exposure: Class C felony (10 years) for providers giving puberty blockers, hormones or surgery to anyone under 19, enforceable since 21 Aug 2023 and unchallenged after plaintiffs withdrew; no insurance-exclusion ban; DOJ subpoenaed 'over 20' hospitals for under-19 patient records in summer 2025.
care_services.protection: No statewide protection documented; emergency visitor care restrictions not documented either way; national litigation over October 2025 proposed health rules is unresolved.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor cannot obtain transitional care here — providers face felony exposure — and hospital-record subpoenas raise outing risk if care is sought.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: SB79 frames gender as immutable binary; national orders describe care as 'mutilation' and direct investigation of 'gender ideology'; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; 2025 polling shows 66% support ASAB-only documents and 69% support sports bans; a July 2026 assessment places the unit in the 'legislatively erasing' worst-law group.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The December 2025 reward memo never lists 'radical gender ideology' as a reward criterion and the strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several executive orders are blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both the probability of discovery and the severity of institutional responses (facility refusal, document scrutiny, custody placement) if a visitor is outed.

minors_guardians.exposure: Provider felony for care under 19; national executive order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; school bathroom and sports bans by birth certificate; state polling among lowest nationally for trans-inclusive policies.
minors_guardians.protection: One challenge was withdrawn, but other national orders remain in litigation; municipal nondiscrimination ordinances (two units) offer narrow local cover.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces care denial, school-rule exposure on any campus visit, and heightened document scrutiny for the minor at entry; outing the child also risks the provider-felony environment.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide prohibition on gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing or public accommodations, leaving service denial without state remedy; state hate-crime law (1994) omits gender identity; most trans residents carry wrong-gender daily ID per a civil-liberties group, heightening ID-check exposure; majority polling shows low social support.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute (2009) covers gender-identity bias; 2020 national employment-discrimination ruling and circuit application of gender identity to sex since 2011; two municipalities plus three cities provide local protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If outed on the street, a visitor has federal hate-crime recourse but no state public-accommodations claim outside two municipalities; the 3.8/100k killing figure is an undercount floor on a 2008–2025 base and is not used as evidence of rate.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Statewide complaint machinery for service denial does not exist; courts in this circuit upheld refusal of accurate licences (Sept–Dec 2024) and the surgery requirement, so efficient institutions partly enforce hostile policy; campus-bathroom bill's precise scope and final status of the March 2024 university bill are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Pending civil-liberties litigation on passport markers, enjoined executive orders, national hate-crime and employment statutes, legal-aid FAQ, and functioning federal courts that have blocked several measures.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy depends on forum: federal litigation and hate-crime law operate, while state-level service and facility complaints have no channel, so a visitor's practical recourse varies by actor encountered.

anchor_checks.comparison: Very close: both combine birth-sex facility rules in public buildings, document scrutiny when appearance is questioned, courts rejecting challenges, no offence of being trans, and polite street life. This dossier adds an entry regime capable of refusal or lifetime fraud ineligibility, conversion-style federal custody policy, and majority-poll social support for restrictions, while lacking 0.35-A's wholly uniform single rule; net slightly more exposure.

Higher than this case. 0.45-A has only a birth-sex bathroom rule in publicly funded buildings with a polite public, ordinary emergency care, and one prosecuted assault — no entry/document regime, no custody conversion policy, no statewide service-recourse gap paired with hostile framing. The present dossier's additional tier-1 and tier-2 features justify a materially lower score.

Higher than 0.25-D. That profile has a compulsory birth-sex rule for all public facilities including hospitals with complaints routinely rejected, plus recurrent police stops threatening fraud charges. Here facility scope is government buildings and schools, no police extortion or stops are documented, presentation is not criminalised in this unit, and federal hate-crime and employment protections plus active litigation operate.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a layered regime: entry screening where a document/sex discrepancy can trigger refusal or a fraud-based lifetime bar; government-building facility exclusion federally and school/campus exclusion at state level; a binary-sex statute; no state public-accommodations or hate-crime recourse outside two municipalities; and federal custody where hormones are removed and immigration detainees report abuse. Threat-framing is official and socially backed by majority polling, raising both discovery and severity. Mitigation is real but partial: presentation is not criminalised in this unit, no in-state violence pattern is documented (the 3.8/100k figure is an unusable undercount floor), a federal hate-crime statute and employment ruling exist, and courts have enjoined several national orders. Adults travelling with a minor add felony-level care denial. Net: documented universal and institutional exposures with thin state remedy — Elevated Risk, low end.
